title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
layout_note: Four lettered panels in one row: (a) and (b) are two copies of the same 3-D scene box with camera image planes, (c) stacks two small density-vs-distance plots, (d) stacks two loss expressions. The network sits as a tiny glyph between (a) and (b), not in its own panel.
grouping: Grouping is by panel only: each step has a two-line centred title above it (input, output, rendering, loss) and a letter (a)-(d) below it; no containers or background tints. Panels (c) and (d) are split into a top row for Ray 1 and a bottom row for Ray 2, so the two rays are carried across the last two steps as parallel lanes.
shapes_depth: The scene is a dotted wireframe cube with a faded render of the object inside and two perspective-tilted image planes (photos) on its sides. Camera rays are thin red lines ending in blue open arrowheads at the camera side; sample points along a ray are small dots (black in (a), coloured fills in (b) to show predicted colour). The MLP is three small blue-outlined grey bars labelled F_Theta. Curved blue arrows with filled heads hop from a sample point to the input tuple, from the output tuple into the scene, and from each plot to its loss box. Plots are bare axes with a yellow-to-orange gradient curve. Loss is drawn as a coloured square minus 'g.t.' inside double-bar norm brackets.
proposed_highlight: No box or colour marks the method; the contribution is shown by drawing the data itself: rays through a 3-D scene, sample points coloured by what the network returns, and per-ray density curves. The two named rays are tracked through every panel.
lesson: Draw the radiance-field step inside a wireframe scene cube with real image planes and red rays carrying sample dots, and carry two named rays as parallel lanes into the density plots and the loss so the reader can follow one pixel end to end.
notes: venue from the arXiv comment 'ECCV 2020 (oral)' (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref); year 2020 is the venue year. Rendered objects are part of the figure's raster content.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: four lettered columns (a)-(d) left to right: sample 5D points along rays in the scene, query F_Theta for colour and density, volume-render each ray's curve, compare the rendered pixel with ground truth

relations.form: four unboxed columns each headed by a two-line title and lettered (a)-(d) below, read left to right
(a) and (b) draw the operation on the actual scene: rays through a dotted bounding box of the Lego bulldozer with two real image planes, sample points as dots on the rays
a curved blue arrow lifts one sample point to the tuple (x,y,z,theta,phi), through the three-bar network F_Theta, to (RGB sigma), and down onto the same point in (b)
in (d) each rendered pixel swatch sits inside a squared-norm bar beside 'g.t.', one row per ray, tied by a curved arrow from that ray's curve in (c)
Ray 1 and Ray 2 run as two stacked rows through (c) and (d), each with its own density curve and its own loss term

channels.colour: the yellow-to-red gradient means predicted colour/density consistently: on sample points in (b), on the curves in (c) and on the pixel swatches in (d); blue = the network and its connecting arrows; red = rays
channels.shape: dots = sample points, three bars = the MLP, curves = density along ray distance, swatches in norm bars = rendered pixels
channels.line: solid red arrows = camera rays; curved blue arrows = 'feeds' links between stages
channels.frame: no frames; columns separated by whitespace and lettered captions

quality.strengths: The pipeline is drawn on the data itself: points on real rays through the scene become coloured points, then density curves, then pixels compared with g.t.; one colour gradient follows the same quantity through (b)-(d), and the representations (5D tuple, RGB sigma, per-ray curves, rendered pixel) are all drawn between the operations that make and compare them.
quality.weaknesses: The network F_Theta, though central, is a tiny three-bar glyph floating between (a) and (b); the curved arrows from points to tuples are short but leave the main left-to-right reading for an arc above the scene.

insights.structure: Four captioned columns (a)-(d) left to right: 5D input on a 3D scene with two camera image planes, output colour and density on the same scene, volume rendering plots for two rays, and rendering loss expressions.
insights.data: Rays are red arrows through a dotted bounding box of a Lego bulldozer with sample points as dots, the MLP F_Theta is three small blue bars between the tuples (x,y,z,theta,phi) and (RGB sigma), and density along each ray is a colour-graded curve over ray distance.
insights.emphasis: Colour carries the idea: sample points in (b) take the colour they predict, the curves in (c) are coloured by the same gradient, and the rendered pixel patches in (d) are those colours compared with g.t. in squared-norm bars.
insights.flow: Left to right with curved blue arrows linking a sample point to the input tuple, the network to the output tuple, and each ray's curve to its loss term.

arrangement.units: four unboxed columns each headed by a two-line title and lettered (a)-(d) below
arrangement.inputs_as: a 3D scene sketch with real photo image planes and rays
arrangement.shared: the same scene and rays are reused in (a) and (b)
